title: Rules, Advice and Deduction
description: Menjelaskan aturan, memberi saran, dan membuat kesimpulan logis. Kamu akan belajar must / have to / need to, perbedaan mustn't dan don't have to, should / ought to / had better, serta must / might / can't untuk deduction tentang masa sekarang.
objectives: Menyatakan kewajiban dengan must, have to dan need to dalam present, past dan future
Membedakan larangan (mustn't) dari ketiadaan kewajiban (don't have to / don't need to)
Memberi saran dan peringatan dengan should, ought to dan had better
Membuat deduction tentang masa sekarang dengan must, might/may/could dan can't, serta menjelaskan aturan di sekolah dan tempat kerja

lessons.title: Must and Have To: Obligation
lessons.summary: Menyatakan kewajiban dengan must dan have to, termasuk bentuk past (had to), future (will have to) dan pertanyaan (Do I have to...?).
objectives: Memakai must dan have to untuk menyatakan kewajiban
Memahami perbedaan nuansa antara must (dari pembicara/tulisan resmi) dan have to (dari luar)
Memakai had to dan will have to untuk kewajiban di masa lalu dan masa depan
Membuat pertanyaan dengan Do/Does ... have to ...?
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Must dan have to = kewajiban
Kita memakai **must** dan **have to** untuk menyatakan bahwa sesuatu *wajib* atau *perlu sekali* dilakukan. In many positive present sentences, both are correct: *I must leave now.* / *I have to leave now.*

| | must | have to |
|---|---|---|
| Positive | I/you/she **must** go | I/you **have to** go; she **has to** go |
| Past | — (tidak ada) | I **had to** go |
| Future | — (jarang) | I **will have to** go |
| Question | Must I go? (formal, jarang) | **Do** I **have to** go? / **Does** she **have to** go? |

### Perbedaan nuansa
- **must** often shows the speaker's own feeling: *I must call my mum tonight* (saya sendiri merasa itu penting). Must juga dipakai dalam **aturan tertulis** dan tanda resmi: *Passengers must show their tickets.*
- **have to** usually shows an obligation from outside — aturan, hukum, atau situasi: *I have to wear a helmet at work* (perusahaan yang mewajibkan).

Dalam percakapan sehari-hari, **have to** lebih sering dipakai daripada must.

### Must tidak punya bentuk past
Must only works for the present and the near future. Untuk masa lalu, selalu pakai **had to**:
- ✗ *Yesterday I must work late.*
- ✓ *Yesterday I **had to** work late.*

For the future, use **will have to**: *Next year you'll have to pay for the course.*

### Have to adalah verb biasa
Karena *have to* berperilaku seperti verb biasa, pertanyaan dan negative-nya memakai **do/does/did**:
- *Do you have to work on Saturdays?* — *Yes, I do.*
- *Did she have to wait long?* — *No, she didn't.*
- Perhatikan **has to** untuk he/she/it: *My brother has to get up at 5 a.m.*

### Hati-hati
- Setelah **must** langsung V1, tanpa *to*: ✗ *must to go* → ✓ *must go*.
- Jangan pakai *-s* setelah must: ✗ *She musts* → ✓ *She must*.
- Untuk negative, *mustn't* dan *don't have to* punya arti yang **sangat berbeda** — kita pelajari di lesson berikutnya.

lessons.title: Mustn't vs Don't Have To
lessons.summary: Membedakan larangan (mustn't) dari 'tidak perlu' (don't have to / don't need to / needn't), serta memakai need to untuk kebutuhan.
objectives: Memakai mustn't untuk larangan

Memakai need to dan Do I need to ...? untuk menanyakan kebutuhan

lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Dua negative yang sangat berbeda
In positive sentences, *must* and *have to* are often similar. But in **negative** sentences they have completely different meanings. Ini salah satu kesalahan paling umum bagi pelajar Indonesia.

| Bentuk | Arti | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| **mustn't** (must not) | dilarang; tidak boleh | You **mustn't** use your phone in the exam. |
| **don't have to** | tidak perlu (boleh kalau mau) | You **don't have to** bring a pen — we have plenty. |
| **don't need to** | tidak perlu | You **don't need to** print the ticket. |
| **needn't** | tidak perlu (lebih formal/British) | You **needn't** wait for me. |

### Mustn't = prohibition
**Mustn't** means *it is not allowed* or *it is a bad idea*. Ada larangan atau bahaya: *Children mustn't play near the river.* Dalam bahasa Indonesia biasanya diterjemahkan **tidak boleh** atau **dilarang**.

### Don't have to / don't need to = no obligation
**Don't have to** means *it is not necessary, but you can if you want*. Tidak ada larangan, hanya tidak wajib: *It's a holiday tomorrow, so I don't have to get up early.* (Kalau mau bangun pagi, boleh saja.)

**Don't need to** dan **needn't** artinya sama. For he/she/it: *She doesn't have to... / She doesn't need to...*

### Need to = it is necessary
**Need to** works like a normal verb: *I need to renew my passport.* Questions: *Do I need to book in advance?* — *No, you don't (need to).*

In the past: *We **didn't have to** pay* / *We **didn't need to** pay* = tidak perlu membayar.

### Awas terjemahan 'tidak harus'
Kalimat *Kamu tidak harus datang* biasanya berarti *tidak perlu datang* → **You don't have to come.** Bukan *You mustn't come* (= kamu dilarang datang). Selalu tanyakan: **apakah ini larangan, atau hanya tidak wajib?**
- Larangan → *mustn't* / *can't*
- Tidak wajib → *don't have to* / *don't need to* / *needn't*

### Hati-hati dengan bentuk
- ✗ *You don't need bring* → ✓ *You don't need **to** bring* (need to).
- ✓ *You needn't bring* (needn't langsung V1, tanpa to).
- ✗ *She don't have to* → ✓ *She **doesn't** have to*.

lessons.title: Should, Ought To and Had Better
lessons.summary: Memberi saran dengan should dan ought to, serta saran kuat atau peringatan dengan had better ('d better).
objectives: Memakai should dan ought to untuk memberi saran umum
Memakai had better / had better not untuk saran kuat dengan peringatan
Menghindari kesalahan bentuk seperti had better to atau ought + V1
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Should dan ought to
You already know **should** from A2: *You should drink more water.* **Ought to** has almost the same meaning — memberi saran atau mengatakan apa yang benar/baik dilakukan. *Ought to* sedikit lebih formal dan lebih jarang dipakai dalam percakapan.

| Bentuk | Positive | Negative | Question |
|---|---|---|---|
| should | You **should** rest. | You **shouldn't** worry. | **Should** I call him? |
| ought to | You **ought to** rest. | (biasanya: shouldn't) | (biasanya: Should I ...?) |
| had better | You**'d better** hurry. | You**'d better not** be late. | (jarang) |

Perhatikan: *ought* selalu diikuti **to**: *You ought **to** see a doctor.* Untuk negative dan pertanyaan, penutur biasanya memilih *should*.

### Had better = strong advice + warning
**Had better** (contraction **'d better**) is stronger than should. Kita memakainya untuk situasi **spesifik dan mendesak**, sering dengan konsekuensi buruk jika saran tidak diikuti:
- *We'd better leave now, or we'll miss the train.*
- *You'd better not tell Mum — she'll be angry.*

Meskipun memakai *had*, artinya **bukan past**. It refers to now or the near future.

### Bentuk had better
- **had better + V1** (tanpa *to*): ✗ *You'd better to go* → ✓ *You'd better go*.
- Negative: **had better not + V1**: ✗ *You hadn't better* → ✓ *You'd better not*.
- Jangan pakai had better untuk saran umum: *People should eat vegetables* (umum) — bukan *People had better eat vegetables*.

### Memilih yang tepat
| Situasi | Pilihan terbaik |
|---|---|
| Saran umum, opini | should / ought to |
| Saran mendesak, ada risiko | had better |
| Aturan/kewajiban | must / have to (lesson 1) |

Useful responses to advice: *Good idea, I will.* / *You're right.* / *Thanks, but I don't think that will work.*

lessons.title: Must, Might and Can't: Deduction
lessons.summary: Membuat kesimpulan logis tentang masa sekarang: must (pasti), might/may/could (mungkin), can't (pasti tidak).
objectives: Memakai must untuk kesimpulan yang hampir pasti benar
Memakai can't untuk kesimpulan yang hampir pasti tidak benar
Memakai might, may dan could untuk kemungkinan
Memakai must be + -ing untuk deduction tentang aksi yang sedang terjadi
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Modals untuk deduction
So far in this unit, *must* meant obligation. But modals have a second use: **deduction** — membuat kesimpulan logis berdasarkan bukti (*evidence*). Kita tidak tahu pasti, tetapi kita menebak dengan alasan.

| Seberapa yakin? | Modal | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| ~95% yakin **benar** | **must** | The lights are on. They **must** be at home. |
| ~50% mungkin | **might / may / could** | He **might** be at the gym, or he **could** be at work. |
| ~95% yakin **tidak benar** | **can't** | She **can't** be hungry — she's just had lunch. |

### Must = I'm sure it's true
*Ari has been working for twelve hours. He **must** be exhausted.* Kita tidak bertanya kepada Ari, tetapi buktinya kuat.

### Can't = I'm sure it's not true
The opposite of deduction *must* is **can't**, NOT *mustn't*. Ini penting:
- ✓ *That **can't** be Lina. She's in Singapore this week.*
- ✗ *That mustn't be Lina.* (mustn't = larangan, bukan deduction)

### Might / may / could = it's possible
You learned *might* and *may* in Unit 3 for future possibility. They also work for **present** possibility: *The phone is ringing. It **might** be the delivery driver.* **Could** juga bisa dipakai dalam kalimat positive: *It **could** be my neighbour.* Untuk negative kemungkinan, pakai **might not / may not**: *She might not know about the meeting.*

### Struktur
- **modal + be + adjective/noun**: *He must be tired. / It can't be true.*
- **modal + V1**: *They must live nearby. / She might know the answer.*
- **modal + be + V-ing** (aksi yang sedang berlangsung): *Rudi isn't answering. He **must be driving**.*

### Tips
Deduction selalu butuh **bukti**. Saat menjawab soal, cari petunjuk dalam kalimat: angka, tempat, waktu, kebiasaan. Then decide: sure it's true (*must*), possible (*might/may/could*), or sure it's impossible (*can't*).

sections.summary: For deduction about the present: **must** = I'm sure it's true, **might/may/could** = it's possible, **can't** = I'm sure it's not true. Lawan dari *must* dalam deduction adalah **can't**, bukan *mustn't*. Gunakan **modal + be + V-ing** untuk aksi yang sedang terjadi.

lessons.title: Rules at School and Work
lessons.summary: Menjelaskan aturan di sekolah dan tempat kerja dengan kosakata seperti compulsory, deadline, fine dan dress code, serta be allowed to.
objectives: Memahami dan memakai kosakata tentang aturan di sekolah dan tempat kerja
Memakai be allowed to / not allowed to untuk izin dan larangan
Menggabungkan semua modal di unit ini untuk menjelaskan aturan secara lengkap
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Menjelaskan aturan
When you start a new job or join a new school, someone usually explains the rules. Dalam lesson ini kita menggabungkan semua modal dari unit ini dan menambah kosakata penting tentang **rules and regulations**.

| Arti | Bahasa Inggris | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| wajib | must / have to / it's compulsory | Wearing a helmet is compulsory. |
| tidak wajib | don't have to / it's optional | The training on Saturday is optional. |
| dilarang | mustn't / not allowed to / it's forbidden | You aren't allowed to eat in the lab. |
| boleh | can / be allowed to | Staff are allowed to use the gym. |
| sebaiknya | should / had better | You'd better not miss the deadline. |

### Be allowed to
**Be allowed to + V1** means *have permission*. Kata *be* berubah sesuai subject dan waktu:
- *Students **are allowed to** use the library until 9 p.m.*
- *We **aren't allowed to** wear jeans on weekdays.*
- ***Are** we **allowed to** bring guests?*
- Past: *When I was a child, I **wasn't allowed to** stay up late.*

Think of *be allowed to* as a fixed phrase. Dalam percakapan, **can / can't** juga sering dipakai untuk izin: *You can't park here.*

### Kata-kata penting
- **compulsory** (wajib) ↔ **optional** (tidak wajib)
- **forbidden** (dilarang keras) — sering dipakai dalam tanda: *Smoking is forbidden.*
- **deadline** — batas waktu: *The deadline for the project is Friday.*
- **fine** — denda: *If you park here, you might get a fine.*
- **permit** — surat izin resmi: *You need a permit to fish in this lake.*
- **dress code** — aturan berpakaian; **badge** — tanda pengenal; **overtime** — lembur.

### Menjelaskan aturan dengan lengkap
A good explanation often has three parts: **the rule**, **the reason**, and **the consequence**.
- *You must wear your ID badge at all times **because** the building is very secure. **If** you forget it, security won't let you in.*

Menambahkan alasan membuat penjelasanmu lebih jelas dan sopan. Use *because*, *so*, and first conditional *if* sentences (Unit 4) to explain consequences.

sections.summary: To explain rules, combine **must / have to** (wajib), **don't have to** (tidak wajib), **mustn't / not allowed to** (dilarang), **can / be allowed to** (boleh) and **should / had better** (saran). Kosakata penting: *compulsory, optional, forbidden, deadline, fine, permit, dress code*. Tambahkan alasan dan konsekuensi agar penjelasanmu jelas.

fine = denda; fee = biaya (untuk layanan)

deadline for the project

something you are not allowed to do

questions.explanation: **Compulsory** = wajib. Kalimat ini membandingkannya dengan *optional* (boleh dipilih), jadi artinya adalah sesuatu yang harus dilakukan.

questions.prompt: A new student or employee is joining your school, office or a café you know. Write a short message explaining the most important rules. Use at least five of these: must, have to, don't have to, mustn't, should, had better, be allowed to. Give a reason for some of the rules.
questions.explanation: Contoh kalimat: *You have to arrive by 8 a.m. because the café opens at 8.30. You don't have to wear a uniform, but you mustn't wear shorts. You're allowed to have a free drink during your break.* Periksa bahwa kamu memakai mustn't untuk larangan dan don't have to untuk hal yang tidak wajib.

questions.explanation: Urutan dasar: **subject + have to + V1 + object + keterangan**: *All employees have to wear their ID badges at all times in the building.*

unitTestQuestions.prompt: When my grandfather was young, he ___ walk five kilometres to school every day.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Kebiasaan di masa lalu (*When my grandfather was young*) → **had to**. Must tidak punya bentuk past.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct option for each gap.
unitTestQuestions.text: Employees ___ smoke anywhere inside the building — it's against the law. But they ___ stay late on Fridays; it's optional.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Merokok di dalam gedung dilarang → **mustn't**. Pulang larut pada hari Jumat bersifat *optional* → **don't have to**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete the reply with a modal of deduction.
unitTestQuestions.text: A: Whose jacket is this? It's enormous! B: It ___ be Nadia's. She's very small.
answers: can't
cannot
couldn't
could not
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Nadia sangat kecil, jadi kita yakin jaket besar itu bukan miliknya → **can't** (deduction negative). *Mustn't* tidak dipakai untuk deduction.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it has a similar meaning.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: It's a good idea for us to book a table. The restaurant is always busy on Saturdays.
unitTestQuestions.cue: Use had better. Begin with: We ...
answers: We had better book a table.
We'd better book a table.
We had better book a table. The restaurant is always busy on Saturdays.
We'd better book a table. The restaurant is always busy on Saturdays.
We had better book a table because the restaurant is always busy on Saturdays.
We'd better book a table because the restaurant is always busy on Saturdays.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Saran kuat untuk situasi spesifik → **had better / 'd better + V1** (tanpa to): *We'd better book a table.*

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Against the rules* menunjukkan larangan, jadi harus **mustn't** (atau *aren't allowed to*). *Don't have to* hanya berarti 'tidak perlu'.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Mira has three cats and two dogs, and she volunteers at an animal shelter every weekend. Which deductions are logical? Choose all correct answers.
options: She might want to adopt another pet one day.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Bukti menunjukkan Mira sangat suka hewan → **must love animals** logis, dan mungkin dia ingin hewan lain (**might**). *Can't like animals* dan *must hate dogs* berlawanan dengan bukti.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Pola: **subject + don't need to + V1**: *You don't need to bring your own laptop.* (Tidak perlu membawa laptop sendiri.)

options: Only on Fridays. From Monday to Thursday you have to dress formally.
Only on Fridays. From Monday to Thursday you don't have to dress formally.
Yes, you must wear jeans every day.
Only on Fridays. From Monday to Thursday you'd better to dress formally.
